teaser.text: Legal & General is a financial-services group that turns savings, premiums and investment fees into retirement income, insurance protection and long-term investment services. Its business looks varied, but the money story is consistent: customers pay now, L&G manages risk and assets, and money goes out later as benefits, pensions, loans or operating costs.

stock.title: L&G stock forecast
stock.meta_description: L&G stock forecast: weighted scenarios, key drivers, capital generation and valuation.
stock.opening: L&G's weighted scenario is 270.61 GBp in October 2027. It hinges on book value rebuilding while L&G preserves capital and delivers profitable growth.
stock.closing: The full memo also explains L&G's business, its rivals, its management and its risks.

paragraphs.text: The weighted forecast is a near-term pause followed by substantial recovery. In October 2027, the weighted price is 270.61 GBp, implying a 2% loss with dividends. In October 2028, it reaches 350.65 GBp, implying a 32% total return. By October 2029, it reaches 469.23 GBp, implying an 80% total return.
The forecast assigns the base case a 50% probability. The bear case receives 32%. The bull case receives 18%, because it requires several execution improvements at once.

blocks.heading: What has to go right for L&G, and what could go wrong?

paragraphs.text: The base starts close to today’s 7.68 times, because management targets 6–9% Core Operating EPS growth and delivered 9% growth in 2025. The bear case reflects weaker deal economics, outflows and declining confidence. The bull case requires profitable pension-risk transfer, better asset-management flows and capital generation that supports distributions.

blocks.heading: How much cash does L&G really make?

paragraphs.text: Debt and cash-flow shortcuts are also less useful here. Insurer debt and investment assets are part of the business machinery, while EBITDA does not capture long-term policyholder obligations. Free cash flow does not cleanly represent cash available to shareholders because premiums and investment flows are integral to operations. Capital generation and cash remitted to the parent matter more.

blocks.heading: What does an investor pay for L&G today?

paragraphs.text: The three P/E measures answer different questions. A P/E ratio compares the share price with earnings per share, but insurance earnings include estimates about contracts that may run for decades. IFRS 17 records expected profit for future insurance service and releases it as that service is provided. Reported profit can also include investment movements, restructuring and the gain from selling L&G’s non-retained US business. Core profit aims to show recurring performance more clearly, while forecast profit asks what may happen next.

dividend.title: L&G dividend: cash coverage and outlook
dividend.meta_description: L&G's dividend outlook, cash coverage, payout choices, guidance, risks and current yield in one clear view.
dividend.opening: L&G's forecast dividend per share is 0.23 GBP in 2027 and 2028, rising to 0.24 GBP in 2029. The memo tests coverage through capital generation: H1 net surplus generation was 713 million against dividends paid of 886 million, while new business and buybacks compete for the same resources.
dividend.closing: The full memo also explains L&G's business, its rivals, its management choices and the risks around them.

blocks.heading: Does L&G's dividend come from cash?

paragraphs.text: The base path follows management’s 2% annual dividend-growth guidance through 2027 and extends it modestly. It also assumes surplus generation covers the dividend by 2027. The bear case reflects H1 net surplus generation of 713 million against dividends paid of 886 million, while the bull case assumes stronger fee earnings and surplus generation.

The US disposal released a large amount of capital. L&G directed £1bn of the proceeds to an additional shareholder return and later announced a £1.2bn buyback. A buyback reduces the number of shares claiming future earnings, but it benefits continuing shareholders only if L&G pays a sensible price and retains enough capital for its obligations.

paragraphs.text: The bear case would become more likely through 2027–28 if new pension premiums and CSM weaken further, or if tight spreads force L&G to reject business. Through 2027–29, continuing asset-management outflows or surplus generation below dividends would reduce buybacks, dividend growth and the multiple.

blocks.heading: What is L&G's dividend yield today?

paragraphs.text: The dividend yield is not guaranteed income. It can rise because the share price falls, not because the dividend becomes safer. L&G says core earnings should cover the dividend in 2026 and that cover should improve in 2027. It also plans more than £5 billion of shareholder returns across 2025–2027. Solvency II operational surplus generation was £790 million in the first half of 2026. That supports the plan, but new business and capital requirements compete for the same resources.
